steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Audiences are the groups of people who consume media products. Understanding who they are and how they use media is central to media studies.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Demographic profiling classifies audiences by measurable characteristics: age, gender, income, occupation, education, ethnicity, and location.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Psychographic profiling classifies audiences by personality, values, attitudes, interests, and lifestyles — e.g. 'aspirers', 'reformers', 'mainstreamers'. This is often more useful than demographics for targeting.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Blumler and Katz's Uses and Gratifications theory identifies four needs audiences fulfil through media: information/education, entertainment, social interaction, and personal identity.
